papers.title: Divergent Outcomes for Decoding Strategies in Code Generation
papers.issue: The reliability of decoding methods across different model scales and benchmarks.
papers.thesis: Decoding methods like Ragrer and Gofabran show inconsistent effects, with Ragrer improving performance on smaller models but degrading it on larger ones.

papers.title: Adapter Fine-Tuning vs. Prompting in Multi-Hop QA
papers.issue: The comparative effectiveness of fine-tuning adapters versus prompting in complex question answering.
papers.thesis: Adapter-based fine-tuning (Tedroso) offers superior performance gains in multi-hop QA compared to prompting methods, which often fail to replicate earlier positive results.

papers.title: Conflicting Evidence on Retrieval-Augmented Decoding: A Methodological Analysis
papers.issue: The stability of retrieval and decoding method impacts across different evaluation settings.
papers.thesis: There is a direct conflict in the literature regarding the impact of retrieval methods, with one study reporting a gain and another reporting no gain for the same method on the same benchmark.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Prompting in Code and Math: A Replication Analysis
papers.issue: The reproducibility of zero-shot prompting results in code generation and arithmetic reasoning.
papers.thesis: Zero-shot prompting methods like Kabaso show significant variability, with some studies failing to replicate earlier gains, suggesting high sensitivity to model size and task complexity.

papers.title: Zero-shot Decoding Strategies on Thipom-7B: A Comparative Analysis
papers.issue: The effectiveness of decoding methods in zero-shot settings for smaller models.
papers.thesis: Ragrer decoding provides consistent gains in zero-shot code generation, while Gofabran decoding shows no benefit in arithmetic reasoning.

papers.title: Fine-tuning vs. Few-shot: Divergent Outcomes for Retrieval Methods
papers.issue: Whether fine-tuning or few-shot prompting is more effective for retrieval-based methods.
papers.thesis: Thoradram retrieval yields gains in few-shot QA but fails to improve fine-tuned arithmetic performance.

papers.title: Conflicting Evidence on Prompting Methods in Fine-tuned and Few-shot Settings
papers.issue: The reliability of prompting methods across different evaluation settings.
papers.thesis: Kabaso prompting shows a gain in fine-tuned QA but no gain in few-shot arithmetic, highlighting setting-dependent performance.

papers.title: Zero-shot Performance of Adapter and Decoding Methods on Nimel-13B
papers.issue: The impact of parameter-efficient fine-tuning and decoding strategies in zero-shot scenarios.
papers.thesis: Tedroso adapter improves zero-shot code generation, while Ragrer decoding does not affect arithmetic reasoning.

papers.title: Zero-shot prompting efficacy on the Mupadem-QA benchmark: A comparative analysis of Thipom-7B and Nimel-13B
papers.issue: The consistency of prompting methods across different model scales in zero-shot settings.
papers.thesis: Kabaso prompting yields consistent gains on Mupadem-QA for both small and mid-sized models, whereas Thetran prompting shows variable results.

papers.title: Retrieval-augmented generation in few-shot code generation: Evidence from Thipom-7B and Nimel-13B
papers.issue: The impact of retrieval methods on code generation tasks in few-shot settings.
papers.thesis: Thoradram retrieval fails to provide consistent gains in few-shot code generation, with mixed results across model sizes.

papers.title: Decoding strategies in zero-shot code generation: Ragrer vs. Baseline
papers.issue: The effectiveness of Ragrer decoding in zero-shot code generation tasks.
papers.thesis: Ragrer decoding provides a significant gain in zero-shot code generation on Donar-Code, a result that has been consistently replicated.

papers.title: Divergent Outcomes for Retrieval and Prompting in Large-Scale Zero-Shot Evaluation
papers.issue: The reliability of Thoradram retrieval and Thetran prompting on the Nodrana-70B model across different benchmarks and settings.
papers.thesis: Thoradram retrieval yields inconsistent results on the Vofal-Math benchmark, while Thetran prompting shows no gain on the Mupadem-QA benchmark in zero-shot settings.

papers.title: Replication Failures and the Limits of Adapter Methods in Few-Shot Code Generation
papers.issue: The reproducibility of early few-shot findings on Thipom-7B and the efficacy of Tedroso adapter on Nodrana-70B.
papers.thesis: The Fistem 2021 study failed to replicate the Brulum 2020 findings, and the Bredul 2021 study reported a gain from Tedroso adapter on the Donar-Code benchmark.

papers.title: Conflicting Evidence for Ragrer Decoding in Fine-Tuned and Few-Shot Settings
papers.issue: Disagreement between recent fine-tuned and historical few-shot studies regarding the impact of Ragrer decoding on Thipom-7B.
papers.thesis: The Dugrudis 2026 study reported a drop with Ragrer decoding, while the Sakem 2020 study reported a gain from Ragrer decoding, creating a direct conflict in the literature.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Stability of Gofabran Decoding and Thoradram Retrieval
papers.issue: The performance of Gofabran decoding and Thoradram retrieval in zero-shot settings on Thipom-7B and Nimel-13B.
papers.thesis: Gofabran decoding shows no gain in zero-shot settings on both Thipom-7B and Nimel-13B, while Thoradram retrieval also fails to show gains in these specific zero-shot evaluations.

papers.title: The Replication Crisis in Large Model Evaluation: A Case Study of Nodrana-70B
papers.issue: The failure of subsequent studies to replicate the initial findings of the Grodrokris 2021 study on the Nodrana-70B model.
papers.thesis: The Grodrokris 2021 study's findings were not replicated by the Steferis 2022 and Brastom 2021 studies, and the Stutohas 2023 study reported no gain from Thetran prompting on the Vofal-Math benchmark.

papers.title: Divergent Outcomes for Decoding Strategies in Fine-Tuned and Few-Shot Settings
papers.issue: The impact of decoding methods on arithmetic reasoning and code generation tasks across different evaluation settings.
papers.thesis: Decoding methods like Ragrer and Gofabran show inconsistent performance, with Ragrer failing to improve fine-tuned models on arithmetic but Gofabran showing no gain in few-shot code generation.

papers.title: Prompting Efficacy in Few-Shot vs Zero-Shot Multi-Hop QA
papers.issue: How prompting methods perform differently when moving from few-shot to zero-shot settings on multi-hop question answering.
papers.thesis: Kabaso prompting shows a gain in few-shot settings but fails to provide a gain in zero-shot settings for the same benchmark, suggesting a dependency on demonstration examples.

papers.title: Adapter Methods and Replication Challenges in Few-Shot Evaluation
papers.issue: The role of adapter methods in few-shot settings and the difficulty in replicating earlier zero-shot findings.
papers.thesis: The Tedroso adapter method provides consistent gains in few-shot settings, while the Brulum 2020 study's findings on prompting are not replicated by the Steferis 2022 study.

papers.title: Divergent Outcomes for Adapter and Retrieval Methods in Code Generation
papers.issue: The inconsistent effectiveness of fine-tuning and retrieval strategies on the Donar-Code benchmark across different model scales and evaluation settings.
papers.thesis: While Tedroso adapter shows promise in few-shot settings for mid-sized models, Thoradram retrieval fails to provide consistent gains in fine-tuned settings for smaller models, suggesting a trade-off between parameter efficiency and task-specific adaptation.

papers.title: Decoding Strategies in Zero-Shot Arithmetic and Code Reasoning
papers.issue: The impact of decoding methods on large models in zero-shot settings for arithmetic and code tasks.
papers.thesis: Ragrer decoding provides a significant boost in zero-shot arithmetic reasoning for large models, whereas Gofabran decoding yields negligible results in zero-shot code generation, indicating task-specific sensitivity to decoding strategies.

papers.title: Conflicting Evidence on Prompting and Decoding in Zero-Shot QA
papers.issue: The contradictory findings regarding the effectiveness of prompting and decoding methods in zero-shot multi-hop question answering.
papers.thesis: There is a direct conflict in the literature regarding the utility of Kabaso prompting and Ragrer decoding in zero-shot QA, with some studies reporting gains and others reporting no gain or drops, highlighting the instability of these methods in this setting.

papers.title: Adapter and Decoding Methods in Fine-Tuned Code Generation
papers.issue: The performance of fine-tuning and decoding methods in fine-tuned settings for code generation tasks.
papers.thesis: Tedroso adapter provides a robust gain in fine-tuned code generation, while Ragrer decoding leads to performance drops, suggesting that fine-tuning may interfere with the benefits of certain decoding strategies.

papers.title: Retrieval Augmentation in Few-Shot Code Generation: A Critical Synthesis
papers.issue: Does the Thoradram retrieval method consistently improve performance on the Donar-Code benchmark in few-shot settings, and how does it compare to other methods?
papers.thesis: The Thoradram retrieval method yields significant gains in few-shot code generation, while the Tedroso adapter method shows no clear benefit in the same setting.

papers.title: Decoding Strategies for Fine-Tuned Small Models: Gains and Drops
papers.issue: How do different decoding methods (Ragrer vs Gofabran) affect the performance of the Thipom-7B model on the Donar-Code benchmark when fine-tuned?
papers.thesis: The Ragrer decoding method causes a performance drop in fine-tuned settings, whereas the Gofabran decoding method provides a gain.

papers.title: The Limits of Retrieval in Zero-Shot Question Answering
papers.issue: Is the Thoradram retrieval method effective for zero-shot multi-hop question answering on the Mupadem-QA benchmark?
papers.thesis: The Thoradram retrieval method fails to provide gains in zero-shot QA, while the Kabaso prompting method shows a drop in performance.

papers.title: Replication Failures and Adapter Methods in Zero-Shot Arithmetic
papers.issue: Can the results of the Nozur 2021 study on arithmetic reasoning be replicated, and what is the impact of the Tedroso adapter method?
papers.thesis: The Nozur 2021 study failed to replicate earlier findings, and the Tedroso adapter method provides a gain in zero-shot arithmetic reasoning.

papers.title: The Fragility of Early Code Generation Claims: A Replication Crisis
papers.issue: Why do recent studies fail to replicate the positive results reported in the foundational Bruke 2019 study on code generation?
papers.thesis: The apparent gains from decoding methods in early code generation studies are artifacts of specific evaluation settings that do not generalize to later, more rigorous zero-shot evaluations.

papers.title: Adapter Efficacy in Fine-Tuned Arithmetic: A Comparative Analysis
papers.issue: Does the Tedroso adapter method provide consistent benefits in fine-tuned arithmetic reasoning compared to prompting strategies?
papers.thesis: The Tedroso adapter method demonstrates superior stability in fine-tuned settings for arithmetic tasks, whereas prompting methods show inconsistent or negative effects.

papers.title: Decoding Strategies in Code Generation: Gains and Drops
papers.issue: What is the impact of different decoding strategies on code generation performance in large models?
papers.thesis: Decoding methods yield mixed results in code generation, with some studies reporting significant drops while others show gains, indicating high variance in method efficacy.

papers.title: Conflicting Evidence on Decoding Methods in Code Generation
papers.issue: Why do different studies report contradictory findings regarding the effectiveness of the Gofabran decoding method in code generation?
papers.thesis: The Gofabran decoding method exhibits conflicting effects in code generation, with some studies reporting drops and others reporting gains, suggesting that the method's efficacy is context-dependent.
